title: Do You Know What I'm Going to Say?
title_html:
Do You Know What
I'm Going to Say?
source: The Turkish Jester, tr. George Borrow (1884), anecdote 1
lesson: Help each other learn; knowledge is meant to be shared.
lines: Nasreddin was asked to give a speech to the whole town. He didn't prepare. At all.
Do you know what I'm going to say? he asked. No, said the crowd. Then why should I talk to people who know nothing? And he walked off.
Next week: Do you know what I'm going to say? This time they said, Yes!
Then you already know. Why should I tell you? And he left again.
Third week, the crowd was ready. Half said yes, half said no!
Nasreddin smiled. Wonderful! Then those who know can tell those who don't. And off he went, again.
Lazy? Maybe. But he had a point: knowledge grows when we share it with each other.
Next episode: why camels don't have wings. Follow so you don't miss it!
